title: Get-Command and Get-Help
summary: Find the command you need without leaving the shell, read its examples, and name your own commands the way PowerShell expects.

steps.title: Verb-Noun: names you can guess
body: Every PowerShell command is named **Verb-Noun**: `Get-Process`, `Stop-Service`, `Compress-Archive`, `ConvertTo-Json`.
The verbs come from a fixed list (`Get-Verb` shows all 100), so once you know the noun you can guess the rest:
| Verb | Means | Example |
| `Get` | read, never change | `Get-ChildItem`, `Get-Service` |
| `Set` | change something that exists | `Set-Content`, `Set-Location` |
| `New` / `Remove` | create / delete | `New-Item`, `Remove-Item` |
| `Start` / `Stop` | run / end | `Start-Process`, `Stop-Service` |
| `ConvertTo` / `ConvertFrom` | change format | `ConvertTo-Json`, `ConvertFrom-Csv` |
| `Import` / `Export` | read / write a file of objects | `Import-Csv`, `Export-Clixml` |
| `Test` | answer true or false | `Test-Path`, `Test-Connection` |
So **`Get-Command`** is your search engine:
```powershell
Get-Command -Noun Archive              # every command about archives
Get-Command *json*                     # wildcards on the whole name
Get-Command -Verb Test                 # every Test- command
Get-Command -ParameterName Encoding    # commands that take -Encoding
Get-Command Compress-Archive -Syntax   # just its parameter sets
`Get-Command` also finds **native programs** (`git`, `ssh`, `robocopy.exe`) on the PATH, and tells you which one wins
when two have the same name: `Get-Command sort -All`.

pairs: Which commands can write UTF-8 with a BOM?

steps.title: Get-Help: examples first
body: Help is built in and searchable. The fastest way to learn a command is its **examples**:
```powershell
Get-Help Compress-Archive -Examples        # real examples with explanations
Get-Help Get-Content -Parameter Tail       # one parameter: type, position, pipeline input
Get-Help Get-Content -Parameter T*         # wildcards work: every parameter starting with T
Get-Help about_Comparison_Operators        # concept pages ("about" topics)
Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Online             # the same page on learn.microsoft.com, in a browser
PowerShell ships with only a short **summary** of each command. The full help is downloaded with **`Update-Help`**:
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 installs help for all users by default, so `Update-Help` needs an **administrator** prompt
there (or `-Scope CurrentUser`).
- PowerShell 7 defaults to **`-Scope CurrentUser`**, so any user can run it.
- Run it every few months; on a locked-down server use `Save-Help` on a machine with internet, then
`Update-Help -SourcePath`.
The machine in these lessons has its help already downloaded (it has no internet).

steps.title: Find it, then use it
prompt: Two small jobs, with commands you may not know yet. Find them with `Get-Command` and `Get-Help`, then do the job:
1. Write the **last 20 lines** of `~/logs/app.log` into `~/answers/tail.txt` (like `tail -n 20`, but with
2. Pack everything inside `~/release` into a zip file, `~/answers/release.zip`.

checks.name: tail.txt holds the last 20 lines
checks.fail: `~/answers/tail.txt` should be exactly the last 20 lines of the log. `Get-Help Get-Content -Parameter T*` shows the parameter.

checks.name: release.zip contains the release files
checks.fail: `~/answers/release.zip` should be a zip with `bin/app.sh`, `config/appsettings.json` and `README.md` in it. `Get-Command -Noun Archive` finds the command.

hints: `Get-Command -Noun Archive` finds `Compress-Archive`; `Get-Help Compress-Archive -Examples` shows how to zip a folder's contents.
steps.explain: `Get-Content -Tail` reads from the end of the file, so it is fast even on a 2 GB log; add `-Wait` and it follows the file like `tail -f`. `Compress-Archive -Path folder/*` zips the folder's *contents*; `-Path folder` puts the folder itself at the top of the zip.

steps.prompt: On a new Windows server, `Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Examples` shows no examples, only a note that help is not installed. In Windows PowerShell 5.1 as a normal user, `Update-Help` fails with an access error. What do you do?
options: Run `Update-Help -Scope CurrentUser`, or run it from an administrator prompt
Install the help from the PowerShell Gallery with `Install-Module Help`
Use `Get-Help -Full` instead, which does not need the download
steps.explain: 5.1 writes help into the system-wide module folders by default, which needs admin rights. `-Scope CurrentUser` puts it under your profile. `Get-Help -Online` is the other quick way: it opens the current docs page in a browser.

steps.title: Name your own commands the same way
body: Functions you write should follow the same rules, so teammates (and tab completion) can guess them:
- an **approved verb** from `Get-Verb`: `Get-Report`, not `Fetch-Report`; `Remove-OldLog`, not `Delete-OldLogs`;
`New-Folder`, not `Make-Folder`;
- a **singular noun**: `Get-Customer` even when it returns many customers;
- a prefix for a team's own nouns, to avoid clashes: `Get-ContosoReport`.
`Import-Module` warns when a module exports unapproved verbs, and **PSScriptAnalyzer** (the linter every serious
PowerShell repo runs in CI) reports them as `PSUseApprovedVerbs` and `PSUseSingularNouns`:
```powershell
Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path ./tools.ps1
Get-Verb -Verb Remove      # is it approved, and in which group?

steps.title: Approved verbs for the team's helpers
prompt: to see what the linter thinks.
Rename them to **`Get-Report`**, **`Remove-OldLog`** and **`New-Folder`**, including where the script calls them, so
that `PSUseApprovedVerbs` and `PSUseSingularNouns` report nothing. `pwsh -File ~/scripts/tools.ps1` must still print

Read the file as one string: `$t = Get-Content ~/scripts/tools.ps1 -Raw`. Strings have a `.Replace('old', 'new')` method.
explain: The analyzer may now point out something new: `PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions` on `Remove-OldLog` and
`New-Folder`. Verbs like Remove and New promise that `-WhatIf` and `-Confirm` work. Module 4 shows how to keep that

steps.prompt: Approved verb or not? (`Get-Verb` is the list.)
steps.explain: Use `Get` for Fetch, `Remove` for Delete, `New` for Make and `Test` for Check. `Invoke` (run something) and `Sync` are on the list.
